Diego / Sofia — looping in Jordan for procurement alignment.

Diego: our standard approach is to issue a bridge letter that:
- States the date range covered by the last Type II,
- Affirms there have been no material changes to the control environment since the report, and
- Provides an expected month for the next Type II issuance (we normally give a target quarter, e.g., Q2 2027).

Two internal notes:
- Legal prefers we avoid granular control enumerations in bridge letters; procurement teams sometimes push back and ask for a short appendix referencing the control categories (security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity) instead.
- For PO alignment, if Acme needs the bridge attached at time of PO signature, please confirm the signer and whether you require a notarized or countersigned copy. That affects our 7–10 day timeline.

Sofia — if you can paste your procurement template here I’ll adapt the bridge language directly and aim to provide the adapted draft by Monday EOD (Aug 9).

Marissa Cole
